title: Chapter 260: Performance
html:
A cold draft swept down the corridor, sending blank test papers fluttering through the air. Though the classrooms on either side stood empty, strange noises continued to emerge from them. Kong Xiangming’s and Yang Chen’s groups searched opposite sides and reunited three minutes later at the corridor’s end, before the Sealed Classroom.

“The boss changed the locations again.” Yang Chen’s expression darkened. “How many did you find?”

“None,” Wei Wu answered cheerfully. After all, he had not come to search for name tags.

“Why do you sound so happy about finding nothing?” Wang Dan was blunt by nature. “Yang Chen, I think we should continue alone. They’ll only slow us down.”

“They’ve only just entered and still need time to adjust. The layout is complicated, and the boss understands psychology. His hiding places are ingenious, so finding nothing at first is normal.” Yang Chen also found the pair strange, though he could not identify why. “This classroom should contain at least three name tags. We’ll enter together and finish quickly.”

Yang Chen pushed open the Sealed Classroom door and rushed inside first. “Don’t dawdle. Our seniors specifically warned us to move as fast as possible. The longer we remain, the more likely something terrifying will happen!”

Each medical student took a section. They kept their heads down to avoid the mannequins’ eyes, never touched a figure, and snatched up each name tag the instant they spotted it. Their precise, practiced movements resembled a trained drill. Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming remained in the doorway, studying the mannequins’ varied poses.

“I can sense living spirits inside these mannequins,” Kong Xiangming murmured, softly enough that only Wei Wu could hear.

“Turning living people into toys and denying them peace even after death—this man is cruel.” Fear flickered in Wei Wu’s eyes. “Do you think the mannequins were once his enemies?”

“It cannot be that simple. There are too many. Most are probably innocent victims—perhaps even unfortunate visitors.” Kong Xiangming drew a quiet breath. “So many people disappear from this city each year. Some of them may have become mannequins in this Haunted House. Our target is crueler than we imagined. We must be extremely careful.”

Wei Wu took a wary step back. His gaze settled pityingly on the students. How could they know that the mannequins terrifying them might once have been visitors themselves?

“Come help! Why are you standing there?” After finishing his section, Wang Dan found Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming still outside. His temper flared, sharpening his voice.

“Calm down.” Yang Chen restrained Wang Dan. Despite searching the classroom thoroughly, the three found only two name tags.

“The layout has changed. We need to move faster.” Yang Chen left the classroom carrying the name tags. As he passed Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming, his unease intensified. “Gentlemen, if you intend to cooperate, please show some sincerity.”

“Relying on them is a waste of time. We should trust ourselves.” Wang Dan’s patience had run out. He and Li Xue followed Yang Chen into the bathroom beside the classroom. Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming stayed behind and exchanged a glance.

“Those three students are rather interesting. Should we turn them into mannequins too?” Blood vessels surfaced along Wei Wu’s neck. Kong Xiangming shook his head. “Don’t attract unnecessary attention.”

Yang Chen opened the stall doors one by one and found another name tag in the fifth. The painted eyes inside made him shudder. “This Haunted House is insane.”

“Yang Chen, those two visitors are very strange.” Li Xue was the group’s only woman. Though young, she already possessed the finest qualities of a forensic examiner: courage, caution, and exceptional powers of observation.

“I noticed.” Yang Chen signaled for Li Xue to lower her voice. “They’re far too calm. This is an unfamiliar place, yet they show no nerves. In fact, they seem almost comfortable here.”

“Especially the ugly one. He keeps sinking into thought as though he’s plotting something.” Li Xue nodded. “I don’t think they’re real visitors. Could they be actors from the Haunted House?”

Yang Chen and Wang Dan stiffened as a chill climbed their spines. “That’s entirely possible!”

“According to He San, the boss will do anything to frighten people. Once, he disguised himself as a visitor. Seven people entered the Haunted House, but the photograph showed eight…”

“No wonder they aren’t frightened and haven’t found a single name tag.” The more they discussed the theory, the more certain they became. “Thank goodness we realized it early. If they ambushed us at a critical moment, they might actually scare us senseless.”

“This Haunted House’s obsession with scaring people has gone too far. Where is the humanity?” Yang Chen drew out his notebook and added a fourth taboo—Never trust strangers.

“Even the cleverest fox cannot outwit a skilled hunter. Now that we’ve uncovered their identities, victory is one step closer!” Yang Chen knew how to raise morale. “We’ll pretend we suspect nothing. When they reveal themselves, we’ll show that we knew all along. I cannot wait to see their expressions.”

“Exactly. We’ll concentrate on finding the name tags. That will lower their guard, and if we’re wrong, no one will be embarrassed.”

“Who knew you had to guard against other people in a Haunted House? I thought the 200,000 prize was a publicity stunt, but now it hardly seems large enough.”

“Hurry. We’re on a tight schedule, and lingering here will make them suspicious.” Yang Chen waved the others forward. “We should catch up with the couple too. Their argument will provide the perfect distraction for those two actors.”

Their discussion concluded, the three students left the bathroom. At the first junction in Mu Yang High School, they paused briefly before turning down the corridor toward the Deep Well.

…

Chen Ge carried the recorder to the underground scenario with Gu Feiyu. After enduring the young man’s endless pleas, he relented and did not force him to continue farther.

“Xiao Gu, once I’m below, take several large props from the neighboring scenario and barricade the entrance.” Chen Ge checked his equipment, then entered the parking garage. “Guard the way out. Unless I call you, do not move those props, no matter what you hear down there.”

Gu Feiyu stared at Chen Ge in Doctor Skull-cracker’s costume and could not see a Haunted House actor. His boss looked less like a man preparing to frighten visitors than one setting out to commit murder.
